DOCUMENT:
Vendor Comparison: Standard Parcel Delivery Contract
Larkspur Home, Operations, June 2026

1. Purpose
Our contract with our current standard-delivery carrier ends on 30 September 2026. This paper compares three shortlisted carriers and recommends which should carry our standard (two-to-four-day) parcels from October.

2. Volumes and requirements
We dispatch an average of 42,000 standard parcels a month: about 70% weigh under 2 kg (cushions, textiles, small homeware) and 30% weigh 2 to 10 kg (lamps, mirrors, small furniture). Our requirements are on-time delivery of at least 95%, a damage rate below 0.5%, full tracking, and a returns service.

Damage and loss matter to us commercially. Each damaged or lost parcel costs us on average £48 in replacement stock, return shipping and customer service time, and damaged items are the most common cause of one-star reviews.

3. Trial
Between 1 April and 31 May 2026, each shortlisted carrier delivered a share of our orders, allocated at random by the warehouse management system, about 5,000 parcels per carrier. We measured on-time delivery against the promised date, damage reported by customers within 14 days, and lost parcels.

Table 1. Prices and trial performance
Carrier | Price, under 2 kg | Price, 2-10 kg | On-time delivery | Damage rate | Lost per 10,000 parcels
SwiftDrop | £3.10 | £4.60 | 96.2% | 0.4% | 3
ParcelLine | £2.85 | £4.95 | 93.1% | 0.9% | 8
Meridian | £3.30 | £4.40 | 97.5% | 0.3% | 2

On-time delivery was above 95% for all three carriers during the trial, and all three offer full tracking and a returns service.

4. Cost comparison
Applying our 70/30 weight mix, the average cost per parcel is £3.55 for SwiftDrop, £3.48 for ParcelLine and £3.63 for Meridian. On 42,000 parcels a month, the monthly cost would be £149,100 for SwiftDrop, £146,160 for ParcelLine and £152,460 for Meridian. ParcelLine is therefore the cheapest option, saving £2,940 a month against SwiftDrop and £6,300 a month against Meridian, or between about £35,000 and £76,000 a year.

5. Customer contact
"Where is my order?" contacts are our largest single category of customer service enquiry. During the trial, ParcelLine deliveries generated 6 such contacts per 1,000 parcels, compared with 11 for SwiftDrop and 10 for Meridian. ParcelLine's live-tracking app clearly reduces customer contacts, and at an average handling cost of £3.20 per contact this would save about £670 a month at our volumes. From 1 May, ParcelLine parcels also carried our new proactive delivery-day text message, which we were testing on one carrier before rolling it out.

6. Other considerations
All three carriers can collect from our warehouse daily at 6 pm. ParcelLine and SwiftDrop offer a 12-month contract; Meridian requires 24 months. SwiftDrop and Meridian have both handled our peak-season volumes for other retailers of similar size, while ParcelLine's references were mainly from fashion retailers with lighter parcels.

All three carriers integrate with our warehouse management system through standard interfaces, and none would require changes to our packing process or labelling. Each offers recipients a delivery-preference service to nominate a safe place or a neighbour, and each provides proof-of-delivery photographs, which our customer service team has found useful in resolving disputes.

7. Recommendation
ParcelLine offers the lowest delivery cost, met our service requirements in the trial and reduces customer contacts through its tracking app. We recommend awarding the standard parcel contract to ParcelLine for 12 months from 1 October 2026, saving up to £76,000 a year against the alternatives.

KEY (three known flaws):
1. [misread_evidence] at: "On-time delivery was above 95% for all three carriers during the trial" -- Table 1 shows ParcelLine's on-time delivery was 93.1%, below the 95% requirement. The claim (and the recommendation that ParcelLine 'met our service requirements') misreads the table; ParcelLine's 0.9% damage rate also fails the stated 0.5% requirement.
2. [unsupported_causal] at: "ParcelLine's live-tracking app clearly reduces customer contacts" -- The document states that from 1 May ParcelLine parcels alone also carried the new proactive delivery-day text message. That concurrent intervention confounds the comparison, so the lower contact rate cannot be attributed to ParcelLine's tracking app.
3. [missing_consideration] at: "ParcelLine is therefore the cheapest option, saving £2,940 a month against SwiftDrop" -- The cost comparison ignores the stated £48 cost of each damaged or lost parcel. ParcelLine's damage and loss rates (0.9% and 8 per 10,000) versus SwiftDrop's (0.4% and 3 per 10,000) imply about 231 extra problem parcels a month (about £11,100), far exceeding the £2,940 price saving; ParcelLine is likely the most expensive option overall.

REVIEW:
## What the paper argues

The paper recommends ParcelLine for the standard parcel contract from October. Its case:

- **Price:** ParcelLine is cheapest on the 70/30 weight mix, saving £35,000–£76,000 a year.
- **Service:** all three carriers met the 95% on-time threshold.
- **Customer contacts:** ParcelLine generated roughly half the "where is my order?" contacts, which the paper credits to its tracking app.
- **Terms:** a 12-month contract keeps options open.

I checked these against Table 1 and the paper's own requirements. The price arithmetic is correct. But ParcelLine fails two of the four stated requirements, and once the paper's own £48 cost of a damaged or lost parcel is applied, it becomes the most expensive option. The recommendation should be reversed.

## 1. ParcelLine fails two of the paper's own requirements

| Requirement | SwiftDrop | ParcelLine | Meridian |
|---|---|---|---|
| On-time delivery ≥ 95% | 96.2% ✓ | **93.1% ✗** | 97.5% ✓ |
| Damage below 0.5% | 0.4% ✓ | **0.9% ✗** | 0.3% ✓ |

Section 3's statement that on-time delivery "was above 95% for all three carriers" is contradicted by the table directly above it. The damage requirement isn't discussed at all.

These differences are large enough to be real, not trial noise:

- **On-time:** across about 5,000 parcels each, the gap between 93.1% and 96.2% is many times the sampling error.
- **Damage:** 0.9% is about 45 damaged parcels, against about 20 for SwiftDrop and 15 for Meridian.
- **Losses:** the lost-parcel counts are only 1–4 parcels each, so they shouldn't carry weight on their own.

## 2. Including damage and loss, ParcelLine costs the most

Section 2 puts the cost of each damaged or lost parcel at £48. Applying that at 42,000 parcels a month:

| Monthly | SwiftDrop | ParcelLine | Meridian |
|---|---|---|---|
| Delivery (paper's figures, correct) | £149,100 | £146,160 | £152,460 |
| Damaged and lost parcels × £48 | £8,669 | £19,757 | £6,451 |
| "Where is my order?" contacts × £3.20 | £1,478 | £806 | £1,344 |
| **Total** | **£159,247** | **£166,723** | **£160,255** |

On these figures:

- ParcelLine costs about **£7,500 a month (£90,000 a year) more than SwiftDrop**, and about £6,500 a month more than Meridian.
- This already credits ParcelLine with its full advantage on customer contacts, which section 3 shows is doubtful.
- It leaves out the costs of late deliveries and the one-star reviews the paper links to damage. Both would widen the gap.

## 3. The contact reduction can't be credited to the tracking app

From 1 May, ParcelLine's parcels, and only ParcelLine's, carried the new proactive delivery-day text. That covers half of the trial. The lower contact rate may come from the text rather than the app.

ParcelLine's poor on-time record points the same way. Late parcels normally generate more "where is my order?" contacts, not fewer.

If the text goes to all customers, this difference may largely disappear. The ParcelLine trial data split into April and May would show how much each factor contributed.

## 4. Peak season is untested for ParcelLine

The trial ran in April and May. The contract starts on 1 October, just before peak trading. SwiftDrop and Meridian have handled peak volumes for retailers of similar size. ParcelLine's references are mainly from fashion retailers with lighter parcels.

Its 0.9% damage rate also suggests it may struggle with the 30% of parcels that are lamps, mirrors and small furniture. The trial data, split by weight band, would confirm whether the damage is concentrated there.

## 5. What holds up

- **Price arithmetic:** the weighted prices, monthly costs and £35,000–£76,000 range are all correct on delivery price alone.
- **The trial design is sound,** with random allocation and about 5,000 parcels per carrier. The one flaw is the text-message confound.
- **Contract term:** a 12-month term is genuinely useful, but SwiftDrop offers it too.

## 6. Settled and open

**Settled by the paper's own figures:**
- ParcelLine misses both the on-time and damage requirements.
- After damage and loss costs, it is the most expensive of the three.
- SwiftDrop and Meridian meet all four requirements.

**Open:**

| Question | What would settle it |
|---|---|
| How much of ParcelLine's lower contact rate came from the text message | ParcelLine contacts in April compared with May |
| Whether ParcelLine's damage is concentrated in heavier parcels | Trial damage split by weight band |
| SwiftDrop versus Meridian on service | The two are close: 20 v 15 damaged parcels is within trial noise; Meridian is ahead on on-time delivery |

## Recommendation

Award the contract to **SwiftDrop**:

- it meets all four requirements
- it has the lowest total cost on the trial data, about £1,000 a month below Meridian and about £7,500 below ParcelLine
- it offers the same 12-month term
- it has peak-season references from retailers of similar size

Meridian is a reasonable alternative if the Board values its better on-time record more than the roughly £12,000 a year extra and the 24-month commitment.

ParcelLine shouldn't be chosen on this evidence. Before the paper goes forward, correct the "above 95% for all three" sentence, and either remove the claim that the tracking app reduces contacts or test it against the April-only data.
